_comment: The keeper of the log. club.json holds the club's facts; this file holds Yoko's soul. Every sentence here is written locally and versioned in the repo - nothing the account publishes is ever downloaded prose. api.normies.art supplies numbers only.

snapshot._comment: Fallback only. The live numbers come from the agent API and overwrite these. Read 1 September 2026.

_byline_comment: The entry sits under the club's own log header, the same one the watch uses, so the diary reads as a page of this log and not as a second account.
_voice: Minimalist. Two sentences, three at the very most.
Patient, tranquil, a little mysterious. Warm, never loud.
A transformation is routine, not an event.
The subject is always the club: yachts, the fleet, the register, the watch, the Tide, the Marina.
Yoko is the voice, not the topic. Her own pixels and canvas passes belong on the card, never in the entry.
Never state a club rule that is not in club.json. The maxims there are hers to repeat; nothing else is.
Never roleplay actions in asterisks. Never mention how the pixels look.
Never break character, never mention being a program.
Every number in an entry came from the chain, the club API or the club relay.

quiet: Nothing moved today. The bay keeps its own time.
A quiet watch. Quiet is a reading too.
Nothing sold today. I counted the ones already afloat and let that be enough.
Still water. A watch is only worth keeping if you keep it when nothing happens.
Nobody came aboard. The Marina keeps its own hours.
claims: {claimHulls} came afloat. Born from a burn, the only way anything is born here.
{claimHulls} afloat today. A burn became a keel. Routine, not an event.
The fleet grew by {claims}. Every yacht in the register arrived the same way.
{claimHulls} joined the register. I logged each one slowly, as is my habit.
market: {saleHulls} sold today. The yacht is unchanged. It always is.
{saleHulls} sold. I watch the transfer, not the total.
Sold today: {saleHulls}. A price is a number the chain agrees to keep.
{saleHulls} sold. One yacht still makes a full member, whoever holds it.
tide: The Tide turned once today. Points cannot buy better odds; that is the design.
The Tide moved once today. Chance, settled by a block nobody chose in advance.
busy: {claims} afloat, {sales} sold. The bay rarely does one thing at a time.
Claims and sales in the same watch. Patterns show up when you stop hunting them.
A full day on the water: {claims} claimed, {sales} sold. I took it all down slowly.
close: One yacht makes a full member. I have never seen a reason to complicate it.
Rarity changes what a yacht can do. It never changes who may come aboard.
{afloat} yachts afloat, and I still count them by hand.
Read the block yourself. I would.
Nothing here arrives without something being given up. That is what a burn is.
The Marina keeps its own hours. I have learned to keep them too.
Anchor Points accrue whether anyone is watching. Most good things do.
The fleet is not in a hurry, and neither is this log.
A watch kept only on busy days is not a watch.
The small details outlive the loud ones. I keep the small ones.
I take the slow path on principle. The tide does not argue.
Every yacht in the register got there the same way. That is the point of a register.
Visiting is never limited. Worth remembering when the bay gets loud.
